web/composer/protocol.py:R6:ToolArgument: R6 on `except AttributeError: return None` inside the `ToolArgumentError.code` property. The handler is not a swallow: `BaseException.__getattribute__(self, "_safe_code")` is a deliberate probe for the presence of one `__slots__` backing slot, and `AttributeError` is that probe's ABSENT answer, not a failure. `ToolArgumentError` declares `_safe_code` in `__slots__` and writes it in `__init__` via `BaseException.__setattr__`, so the slot is unset only on an instance whose `__init__` never completed (a `BaseException.__new__` bypass, or a partially-constructed instance surfacing from an exception raised mid-`__init__`); on such an instance the class's audit contract still has to project a value, because `safe_message`/`args` are composed on EVERY read and are echoed verbatim to the LLM API and recorded in the Landscape audit trail via the synthetic `role: tool` chat message. The value returned is the closed-vocabulary absent sentinel `None` — the declared type of the property is `str | None` and `None` is `code`'s own "no discriminant" member, so nothing is fabricated and no Tier-3 value can reach the echo through this path. Re-raising instead would replace a bounded audit record with an `AttributeError` escaping a property read during exception handling. The controls that make the swallow safe, by symbol: `ToolArgumentError.__init__` (writes all four `_safe_*` slots before `_tool_argument_error_sealed`), `ToolArgumentError.__setattr__` / `__delattr__` (reject every write and every delete of a `_FROZEN_ATTRS` member after construction, so the slot cannot be removed at runtime), `ToolArgumentError.__init_subclass__` (raises `TypeError`, so no subclass can widen the storage), and the post-handler revalidation in the same property body (`type(value) is str and len(value) <= _MAX_TOOL_ARGUMENT_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS and value in _TOOL_ARGUMENT_ERROR_CODES`), which independently reduces any surviving slot content to `None` unless it is a member of the closed `_TOOL_ARGUMENT_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary. The sibling properties `argument`, `expected` and `actual_type` carry the identical probe with their own fixed fallbacks (`"tool argument"`, `"a valid value"`, `"invalid value"`). Invalidated if `_safe_code` stops being a declared slot written unconditionally by `__init__`, if the post-handler membership check against `_TOOL_ARGUMENT_ERROR_CODES` is removed, or if `code` acquires a meaning in which `None` is no longer the honest absent value.
web/composer/guided/state_machine.py:R5:: R5 `isinstance(sample_rows_value, Sequence)` in `SourceIntent.__post_init__`. `SourceIntent` is a frozen dataclass whose `sample_rows` field is a CONSTRUCTOR PARAMETER, so this runs at the seam where an unvalidated caller value first enters the owned type — including `SourceIntent.from_dict`, which rebuilds an intent from a persisted guided session record, and `chat_solver`'s Step-1 resolution of planner-derived rows. The declared field type is `Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]`, an abstract container protocol with no owned concrete class to name, so ADR-032's "nominally type what ELSPETH owns" has no target here: `type(x) is tuple` would reject the `list` that `from_dict` legitimately passes (`sample_rows=tuple(samples_raw)` is built in `from_dict`, but the dataclass is also constructed directly with lists in the tool path), and the abstract `Sequence` registration is exactly what the check must consult. The paired `isinstance(..., (str, bytes, bytearray))` on the same line is the standard str-is-a-Sequence exclusion. This is a hard rejection, not a masking default — it raises `TypeError("SourceIntent.sample_rows must be a sequence[mapping]")`, and the same shape is used by the sibling owned type `SourceResolved.__post_init__` in `guided/resolved.py` and by `freeze_guided_str_sequence`. The check is load-bearing before the length assertion on the next statement: `len()` on a non-sized value would raise an untyped `TypeError` from a builtin instead of the named contract violation. Invalidated if `sample_rows` is narrowed to one owned concrete type at every construction site, at which point the exact-type form becomes correct.

R5 `isinstance(sample_rows_value, (str, bytes, bytearray))` in `SourceIntent.__post_init__` — the second operand of the same guard as the entry above. `str`, `bytes` and `bytearray` all register as `Sequence`, so a bare `Sequence` acceptance would admit a string and then iterate it character by character; this operand is the exclusion that makes the first one mean "sequence of rows". It must stay `isinstance` rather than `type(x) in {str, bytes, bytearray}` because the exclusion has to catch SUBCLASSES too — a `str` subclass is still a character sequence and must be rejected on the same ground, whereas the exact-type form would let it through into the row loop. Tier of the value: the same constructor-parameter Tier-3 seam described above. It protects the same invariant and raises the same `TypeError`. The identical two-operand idiom appears in `SourceResolved.__post_init__` (`guided/resolved.py`), `freeze_guided_str_sequence`, and `reorder_reviewed_components` (`guided/stage_transitions.py`). Invalidated only if the str-exclusion moves into a shared owned helper that both call.

R5 `isinstance(row, Mapping)` in the `any(...)` element check of `SourceIntent.__post_init__`. Per-element validation of a constructor parameter: each member of `sample_rows` must be a mapping before it is frozen. `Mapping` is an abstract protocol and the field's declared element type, and the reachable domain genuinely includes more than one concrete class — `from_dict` passes plain `dict`s decoded from the persisted record, while a session round-tripped through `freeze_guided_json_mapping` carries `MappingProxyType` values, and `type(x) is dict` would reject exactly the frozen form the class itself produces. The check raises `TypeError("SourceIntent.sample_rows must contain mappings")` — a hard rejection with no default. It is not redundant with the freeze loop that follows: `freeze_guided_json_mapping` is called per row two statements later and would itself raise on a non-mapping, but only AFTER `GuidedJsonBudget` has been charged for the earlier rows, so removing this check would make the error a budget-order-dependent one and change which of two contract messages a malformed record produces. Note also that the tier_model dataflow walk cannot suppress this site even under a boundary decorator: the element name is bound by a genexp loop variable, which the walk does not track (recent-code-hints 2026-08-29). Invalidated if the row element type is narrowed to one owned concrete class at every construction site.

R5 `isinstance(mapping, Mapping)` in `GuidedSession.__post_init__`'s four-way component-collection loop (`reviewed_sources`, `pending_source_intents`, `reviewed_outputs`, `pending_output_intents`). These are constructor parameters of the frozen `GuidedSession` dataclass, reached from `GuidedSession.from_dict` (persisted guided session record) and from every `dataclasses.replace` in `guided/stage_transitions.py`, so the value's type is a caller fact, not a construction guarantee. `Mapping` is the declared field type and the abstract protocol is what must be consulted: the reachable domain spans plain `dict` (built by the transitions and by `from_dict`), the `dict` this same `__post_init__` re-installs via `_validated_component_mapping`, and any read-only view a caller supplies — the file's own comment records that a supplied `Mapping` may be a view over mutable storage, which is precisely why the value is detached and re-frozen rather than retained. `type(x) is dict` would reject a `MappingProxyType` view that the class deliberately accepts and then snapshots. The check raises `TypeError(f"GuidedSession.{field_name} must be a mapping")` — hard rejection, no default. It guards the `set(...)` cardinality assertions on the immediately following statements, which would otherwise raise an unnamed builtin `TypeError`. Invalidated if all four fields become one owned concrete collection type at every construction site.

R5 `isinstance(value, Mapping)` at the head of `GuidedSession._validated_component_mapping`. The parameter is declared `value: object` — the function's entire job is to turn an unvalidated caller value into an owned `dict[str, _ComponentT]` with canonical UUID-text keys and exact-typed values, which is the ADR-032 "parse what it does not own" shape, and this is its type gate. It cannot be `type(x) is dict` for the same reason as its caller above: `GuidedSession.__post_init__` passes whatever the constructor received, which legitimately includes a `MappingProxyType` view. Note the deliberate ASYMMETRY inside this function and why it is correct: the container test is structural (`isinstance(..., Mapping)`) because the container is a protocol ELSPETH does not own, while the per-item test one line below is the exact-type form `type(item) is not item_type` because `item_type` is always an owned concrete class (`SourceResolved`, `SourceIntent`, `SinkOutputResolved`, `SinkIntent`) and those component types are closed — a subclass must not silently pass as its parent inside a session that is later content-hashed. The check raises `TypeError(f"GuidedSession.{field_name} must be a mapping")` — hard rejection. It protects the `value.items()` iteration on the next statement. Invalidated if the four component collections are narrowed to one owned concrete mapping type at every call site.
web/composer/guided/stage_transitions.py: R5 `isinstance(stable_ids, Sequence)` in `reorder_reviewed_components`. The parameter is declared `stable_ids: object` precisely because it arrives from the guided respond route carrying a client-submitted reorder — Tier-3 input, and this function is where it is parsed. `Sequence` is the abstract protocol the ordering contract needs and there is no owned concrete class to name: the route decodes a JSON array to a `list`, the unit tests pass `tuple`s, and both are legitimate. The exact-type form would have to enumerate `{list, tuple}` and would still be wrong for any other registered sequence a caller may hold. The check raises `TypeError("stable_ids must be a sequence of UUID values")` — a hard rejection with no default, pinned by `tests/unit/web/composer/guided/test_stage_transitions.py::test_reorder_reviewed_components_rejects_non_permutations` and `::test_reorder_reviewed_components_requires_stable_id_exact_permutation`. It is load-bearing before the `any(type(stable_id) is not UUID ...)` element check and the `len()`/`set()` permutation assertion that follow: those would raise unnamed builtin errors on a non-sequence. The element check on the next line is deliberately the exact-type form, because `UUID` is a concrete owned-by-stdlib value type whose subclasses must not pass — the same structural-container / nominal-element split as `_validated_component_mapping`. Invalidated if the route is changed to hand this function an already-owned sequence type.

R5 `isinstance(stable_ids, (str, bytes, bytearray))` in `reorder_reviewed_components` — the second operand of the guard above, excluding the text types that also register as `Sequence`. Without it a submitted JSON string would be accepted as a sequence and iterated per character, and every character would then fail the `type(stable_id) is not UUID` element check with the wrong contract message; worse, an empty string would pass the container test and reach the permutation comparison as an empty ordering. It must remain `isinstance` rather than an exact-type set so that `str` SUBCLASSES are excluded on the same ground — an exact-type test would let one through into the element loop. Same Tier-3 client-submitted value, same hard `TypeError("stable_ids must be a sequence of UUID values")`, same pinning tests as the entry above. This is the same two-operand idiom used by `SourceIntent.__post_init__`, `SourceResolved.__post_init__` and `freeze_guided_str_sequence`. Invalidated only if the str-exclusion is factored into a shared owned helper.
